items.title: Perioperative Camrelizumab Plus Chemotherapy in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Despite multimodal treatment, recurrence remains common in patients with resectable locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Whether perioperative chemoimmunotherapy improves long-term outcomes remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the effect of perioperative camrelizumab plus chemotherapy on event-free survival (EFS) compared with standard surgery-based treatment in patients with resectable locally advanced HNSCC.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The CAMORAL trial was a multicenter, phase 2 randomized clinical trial conducted at 4 academic hospitals in China between October 2020 and March 2024, with data cutoff on April 11, 2025. Patients aged 18 to 75 years with untreated, resectable stage III to IVB HNSCC were assigned to neoadjuvant-adjuvant treatment or control. Analyses used the intention-to-treat population. Data were analyzed from May 2025 to February 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized (1:1) to receive two 21-day cycles of neoadjuvant camrelizumab, 200 mg, plus albumin-bound paclitaxel and carboplatin followed by surgery, risk-adapted adjuvant therapy, and maintenance camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles; or upfront surgery followed by standard risk-adapted adjuvant therapy.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was 2-year EFS. Secondary end points included major pathological response (MPR), pathological complete response (pCR), overall survival, 2-year distant metastasis-free survival, 2-year locoregional recurrence-free survival, and safety.
RESULTS: Of 125 included patients, 99 (79.2%) were male, and the mean (SD) age was 56.3 (11.7) years. A total of 63 patients were assigned to the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group and 62 to the control group; the median (IQR) follow-up was 24.6 (16.8-36.5) months. A total of 103 (82.4%) had oral cavity primary tumors. Among 125 patients, the 2-year EFS rate was 77.8% (95% CI, 63.6-87.0) in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group compared with 46.1% (95% CI, 31.3-59.6) in the control group (hazard ratio, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.17-0.68; P = .001). MPR and pCR were 47.6% (95% CI, 34.9-60.6) and 25.4% (95% CI, 15.3-37.9), respectively, in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group, with no MPR or pCR events in the control group. The 2-year overall survival rates were 92.0% and 69.1%, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.25; 95% CI, 0.10-0.64); the hazard ratio of 2-year distant metastasis-free survival was 0.15 (95% CI, 0.03-0.68). Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 50 of 63 patients (79.4%) in the neoadjuvant-adjuvant group and 35 of 62 patients (56.5%) in the control group; 1 fatal treatment-emergent adverse event occurred in the control group.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this phase 2 randomized clinical trial, perioperative camrelizumab plus chemotherapy significantly improved EFS with manageable toxic effects, supporting evaluation of intensified perioperative immune priming in resectable HNSCC.

items.title: Izalontamab Brengitecan in Recurrent or Metastatic Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: The PANKU-Esophagus01 Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Effective therapy remains lacking for patients with advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) whose disease progressed after standard treatment. Izalontamab brengitecan, an epidermal growth factor receptor and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate with a topoisomerase I inhibitor, Ed-04, has shown clinical activity in ESCC in a phase 1b study.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of izalontamab brengitecan compared with chemotherapy in patients with advanced ESCC who progressed after first-line programmed cell death 1 protein (PD-1)/programmed cell death 1 ligand 1 (PD-L1) inhibitor plus platinum-containing chemotherapy.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This phase 3, open-label, randomized clinical trial was conducted across 80 hospitals in China. Patients with recurrent or metastatic ESCC that had progressed with first-line PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor plus platinum-containing chemotherapy were enrolled. Between March 19, 2024, and August 1, 2025 (final follow-up, October 17, 2025), a total of 704 patients were screened, and 497 were enrolled and randomized.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either izalontamab brengitecan (n = 249; 2.5 mg/kg on days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks) or physician-selected chemotherapy (n = 248; irinotecan, paclitaxel, or docetaxel) every 3 weeks.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The dual primary end points were progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 and overall survival (OS).
RESULTS: Of 497 patients who underwent randomization (median age, 61.0 years [range, 34-76]; 448 male patients [90.1%]), 493 received study treatment. At this interim analysis, izalontamab brengitecan demonstrated statistically significant improvement in both PFS and OS. Median PFS by blinded independent central review was 4.17 months (95% CI, 3.61-4.53 months) with izalontamab brengitecan vs 1.97 months (95% CI, 1.61-2.73 months) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.40-0.63; log-rank P < .001). Median OS was 9.79 months (95% CI, 7.89-11.01 months) with izalontamab brengitecan vs 7.20 months (95% CI, 6.18-7.82 months) with chemotherapy (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.48-0.82; log-rank P < .001). Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 212 of 249 patients (85.1%) with izalontamab brengitecan and 147 of 248 patients (59.3%) with chemotherapy and were predominantly hematologic.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Izalontamab brengitecan significantly improved PFS and OS vs chemotherapy in patients with recurrent or metastatic ESCC whose disease had progressed after first-line treatment. These findings support izalontamab brengitecan as a new second-line treatment for this population in China.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06304974.

items.title: Intismeran Autogene plus Pembrolizumab for Resected Stage IIB to IV Melanoma.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intismeran autogene (intismeran) is an individualized neoantigen therapy that is designed to induce new T-cell responses and expand preexisting T-cell responses against patient-specific tumor neoantigens, which may potentially improve the efficacy of adjuvant therapy in patients with melanoma.
METHODS: In this phase 3, double-blind trial, we randomly assigned patients with completely resected stage IIB to IV cutaneous melanoma in a 2:1 ratio to receive intramuscular intismeran (at a dose of 1 mg) or placebo every 3 weeks for nine doses; all the patients received intravenous pembrolizumab (at a dose of 400 mg) every 6 weeks for nine cycles. The primary end point was investigator-determined recurrence-free survival, assessed in a time-to-event analysis. Key secondary end points included investigator-determined distant-metastasis-free survival (assessed in a time-to-event analysis) and safety.
RESULTS: A total of 1137 patients underwent randomization: 757 to the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 380 to the placebo-pembrolizumab group. The median follow-up was 24.6 months. Recurrence-free survival at 24 months was 82.2% in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 70.0% in the placebo-pembrolizumab group (two-sided P<0.001); the piecewise hazard ratio was 0.99 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 1.49) before 6 months and 0.42 (95% CI, 0.30 to 0.58) after 6 months. Distant-metastasis-free survival at 24 months was 88.5% with intismeran-pembrolizumab and 80.2% with placebo-pembrolizumab (two-sided P = 0.002); the piecewise hazard ratio was 1.01 (95% CI, 0.58 to 1.79) before 6 months and 0.50 (95% CI, 0.34 to 0.73) after 6 months. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 23.6% of the patients in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group and 20.3% of the patients in the placebo-pembrolizumab group. Eight patients (1.1%) in the intismeran-pembrolizumab group died from an adverse event; five of the deaths occurred before intismeran was administered.
CONCLUSIONS: Adjuvant therapy with intismeran plus pembrolizumab significantly prolonged recurrence-free survival and distant-metastasis-free survival as compared with pembrolizumab alone in patients with completely resected, high-risk cutaneous melanoma. (Funded by Merck Sharp and Dohme and Moderna; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05933577.).

items.title: Early vs Routine Oral Nutritional Supplementation During Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Oral nutritional supplementation (ONS), providing supplementary oral nutrition in addition to usual food, is widely used during concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), but its optimal timing and cost utility remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate efficacy and explore cost utility of early ONS in patients with NPC undergoing CCRT.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, open-label, randomized clinical trial was conducted at 6 Chinese tertiary hospitals from July 2021 to May 2025. Eligible patients were aged 18 to 70 years with newly diagnosed stage II to IVA NPC, a Patient-Generated Subjective Global Assessment (PG-SGA) score of 0 to 8, and planned CCRT. Key exclusions included oral intake less than 60% of requirements for 3 days or longer, inability or unwillingness to receive concurrent chemotherapy, and inability to receive oral or enteral nutrition. Data were analyzed from November 2025 to March 2026.
INTERVENTION: Participants were randomized 1:1 to early ONS at CCRT start or routine ONS after prespecified nutritional decline.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was the incidence of more than 5% weight loss from baseline to CCRT completion. Secondary end points included PG-SGA score, the incidence of grade 3 or higher radiation-induced oral mucositis (RIOM), quality of life (European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30), and radiotherapy interruption. Cost utility measures included total cost, utility, and incremental cost utility ratio.
RESULTS: Of 242 patients screened, 236 patients were randomized, and the prespecified modified intention-to-treat population included 216 patients (mean [SD] age, 46.62 [11.19] years; 168 [77.8%] male), with 107 receiving early ONS and 109 receiving routine ONS. More than 5% weight loss occurred in 70 participants (65.4% ) in the early ONS group, compared with 88 participants (80.7%) in the routine ONS group (relative risk [RR], 0.81; 95% CI, 0.68-0.96; P = .01). An intention-to-treat analysis including all randomized participants yielded a similar estimate (RR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.65-0.93). In the modified intention-to-treat population, grade 3 or higher RIOM occurred in 15 participants (14.0%) in the early ONS group vs 29 participants (26.6%) in the routine ONS group (RR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.30-0.93). Best-case costs were $9560.56 in the early ONS group vs $9685.23 in the routine ONS group, with quality-adjusted life-years of 0.1144 vs 0.1132, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This randomized clinical trial found that early ONS reduced clinically meaningful weight loss during CCRT; exploratory analyses suggested potential benefits for severe RIOM and a potentially favorable short-term economic profile.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04823468.

items.title: Effect of two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens on the gut microbiome in a randomized phase 3 trial.
items.abstract: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation can cure certain hematological disorders but has many complications. In retrospective studies, low gut microbiome diversity is associated with adverse clinical outcomes. In 2023, the Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1703 randomized phase 3 trial demonstrated the superiority of post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) and mycophenolate mofetil to tacrolimus and methotrexate (Tac/MTX) for graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis in participants with hematological malignancies undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation. Here we report on the microbiome-focused companion study to 1703, Blood and Marrow Transplant Clinical Trials Network 1801, which coenrolled participants and shared trial registration. The primary endpoint was association between microbiome diversity at neutrophil engraftment and non-relapse mortality after 1 year; secondary endpoints included associations with other clinical outcomes and with baseline microbiome diversity. Based on 2575 longitudinally collected stool samples from 304 participants (Tac/MTX n = 147, PTCy n = 157), no association between engraftment microbiome diversity and non-relapse mortality was observed (P = 0.314), not meeting the primary endpoint. Lower baseline microbiome diversity was associated with shorter overall survival (P = 0.007). Safety data were reported in the original 1703 publication. In exploratory analyses, microbiome diversity and absolute microbial load were lower in PTCy compared to Tac/MTX on days 14-28 following HCT, independent of non-prophylaxis antibiotics exposure. Microbial domination events, when a single species exceeds 30% relative abundance, did not differ significantly between study arms and reflected both pathogen blooms and less severe disruptions of the microbial community. Clostridium scindens and secondary bile-acid metabolism pathways were less prevalent in PTCy than in Tac/MTX following HCT. In summary, we find prophylaxis regimens likely exert independent effects on both the microbiome and immune compartments and can also impact their interaction. Understanding whether and how microbiome-targeted interventions might improve transplant outcomes will therefore require careful disentangling of these effects within each specific treatment context. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03959241 .

items.title: Prasugrel versus Ticagrelor in Acute Coronary Syndromes.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether prasugrel or ticagrelor should be the preferred P2Y12 inhibitor for patients with an acute coronary syndrome is uncertain.
METHODS: We conducted a registry-based, open-label, stepped-wedge, cluster-randomized trial in Sweden involving adults who had undergone percutaneous coronary intervention for an acute coronary syndrome. Seven regions, grouped into three clusters, switched from ticagrelor to prasugrel as the default P2Y12 inhibitor in a randomized sequence across four 9-month periods between 2021 and 2024. The primary end point was a composite of death from any cause, fatal or nonfatal myocardial infarction, or fatal or nonfatal stroke through 1 year, as ascertained from national registries. In the intention-to-treat analysis, a mixed model adjusted for cluster and calendar time was used to obtain a policy-level estimate.
RESULTS: A total of 17,095 patients were enrolled; 9444 received care under the default ticagrelor policy, and 7651 received care under the default prasugrel policy. The mean (±SD) age of the patients was 69.8±11.5 years, and 36.8% were at least 75 years old; 27.8% of the patients were female. A total of 39.4% presented with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), 43.7% with non-STEMI, and 16.8% with unstable angina. At 1 year, a primary end-point event had occurred in 11.8% of the patients in the ticagrelor-policy group and in 11.1% of those in the prasugrel-policy group (adjusted odds ratio [prasugrel vs. ticagrelor], 0.90; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.77 to 1.06), and major bleeding had occurred in 4.4% and 4.2%, respectively (adjusted odds ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.64 to 0.99).
CONCLUSIONS: In an unselected population of patients with an acute coronary syndrome who had undergone percutaneous coronary intervention, the risk of ischemic events was not lower with a default prasugrel policy than with a default ticagrelor policy. (Funded by Region Västra Götaland; SWITCH-SWEDEHEART ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05183178.).

items.title: Rivaroxaban Then Aspirin vs. Aspirin Alone after Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aspirin after an initial short course of rivaroxaban has been shown to be safe and effective for the prevention of venous thromboembolism after total hip or total knee arthroplasty, but uncertainty remains about the use of aspirin alone.
METHODS: In this multicenter, double-blind, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients to receive once-daily thromboprophylaxis with either 81 mg of aspirin or 10 mg of oral rivaroxaban for the first 5 days after total hip or total knee arthroplasty. All the patients then received further thromboprophylaxis with 81 mg of aspirin daily for 9 additional days after knee arthroplasty and for 30 additional days after hip arthroplasty. Patients were followed for 90 days for symptomatic venous thromboembolism, which consisted of either proximal deep-vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (primary effectiveness outcome), and for bleeding complications (primary safety outcome). The noninferiority margin for aspirin alone as compared with rivaroxaban-aspirin was 0.7 percentage points.
RESULTS: A total of 5429 patients underwent randomization. Venous thromboembolism developed in 13 of 2718 patients (0.48%) in the aspirin-alone group and in 12 of 2647 patients (0.45%) in the rivaroxaban-aspirin group (risk difference, 0.02 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.34 to 0.39; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Major bleeding or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding events occurred in 45 of 2718 patients (1.66%) in the aspirin-alone group and in 54 of 2647 patients (2.04%) in the rivaroxaban-aspirin group (risk difference, -0.38%; 95% CI, -1.11 to 0.34).
CONCLUSIONS: After total hip and total knee arthroplasty, the use of aspirin alone was not inferior to a strategy of using rivaroxaban followed by aspirin for the prevention of symptomatic venous thromboembolism, with no clinically relevant difference in bleeding events. items.title: Ravulizumab in IgA Nephropathy - Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with IgA nephropathy, complement activation drives glomerular inflammation, which leads to hematuria, proteinuria, and nephron loss. Ravulizumab is a terminal complement inhibitor that prevents formation of C5a and C5b-9.
METHODS: In this phase 3 trial, we enrolled adults with IgA nephropathy who had an estimated glomerular filtration rate of at least 30 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and proteinuria (24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio [with protein and creatinine both measured in grams] of ≥0.75 or total urinary protein excretion of ≥1.0 g per day), despite standard therapy. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive an intravenous infusion of either ravulizumab or placebo every 8 weeks. In the prespecified interim analysis, the primary efficacy end point was the change from baseline in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 34. Safety was also assessed.
RESULTS: In all, 485 patients underwent randomization, with 240 patients assigned to the ravulizumab group and 245 to the placebo group; 352 patients (176 in each group) were included in the interim analysis. In the ravulizumab group, the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at baseline and at week 34 was 1.56 and 0.83, respectively; in the placebo group, it was 1.60 and 1.48, respectively. At week 34, a significant reduction in the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio was observed with ravulizumab (-46.6%) as compared with the reduction observed with placebo (-5.6%), corresponding to an adjusted geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio that was 43.4% (99% confidence interval, 30.1 to 54.2) lower with ravulizumab than with placebo (P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 69.5% of the patients receiving ravulizumab and in 75.8% of those receiving placebo; serious adverse events occurred in 4.6% and 9.0%, respectively. No meningococcal infections or deaths occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: In adults with IgA nephropathy, ravulizumab resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo at week 34. (Funded by Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease Unit; I CAN ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06291376; EU Clinical Trials number, 2023-507851-31-00.).

items.title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Accommodations, Behavior Therapy, and Stimulant Medication: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Although widely deployed, little is known about the efficacy of academic accommodations for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), alone or in combination of behavior therapy and stimulant medication.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of academic accommodations alone and in combination with behavioral interventions and stimulant medication.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a crossover randomized clinical trial with participants introduced to all conditions. Children with ADHD were enrolled in kindergarten through sixth grade. Academic accommodations were changed daily in a randomized order. Stimulant medication and placebo alternated weekly. The general classroom and enhanced behavior classroom intervention alternated every 2 weeks. The study was conducted in summer treatment program classrooms. For the present study, behavior was evaluated in (1) a classroom period where participants completed independent assignments and (2) a classroom period where participants were taught a lesson, completed small group cooperative tasks related to the lesson, and then took a quiz. Study data were analyzed from March to July 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: The single and combined effects of academic accommodations, behavior therapy, and stimulant medication (methylphenidate, 0.3 mg/kg) were evaluated. Academic accommodations were extended time on tasks, frequent breaks during tasks, a low-distraction workspace, and the ability to stand at the desk, compared with a condition without an accommodation. A general classroom setting was compared with a classroom setting with enhanced behavior intervention.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Main outcomes were classroom rule violations during each of the two, 1-hour class periods, the number of seatwork items completed correctly (ie, academic productivity), and the quiz score.
RESULTS: Of 306 children screened, 280 were enrolled in the study. A total of 255 children (mean [SD] age, 8.8 [1.6] months; 201 male [79%]) started the intervention, and 235 (84%) completed the study. Compared with placebo, stimulant medication increased effects related to seatwork productivity by 22% (ie, the rate ratio [RR] for this condition indicated that receiving medication compared with placebo multiplied the expected count of problems completed per minute by 1.22; 95% CI, 1.19-1.25), and quiz scores were significantly improved by 3.9 points (95% CI, 3.10-4.70 points). Medication and behavioral therapy significantly reduced classroom rule-breaking behavior by 37% (RR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.60-0.67) and 61% (RR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.37-0.42), respectively. There was no evidence that any of the academic accommodations significantly improved behavior or academic outcomes. No interactions were significant.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this crossover randomized clinical trial question whether school-based academic accommodations for children with ADHD should continue to be emphasized as accommodations were ineffective when used alone or in combination with other ADHD treatments. Results support the continued use of behavioral and pharmacological treatment for ADHD.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05469386.

items.title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results.
METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points.
RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results.
CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

items.title: Treatment of Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Review.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Acute ischemic stroke, caused by thrombotic or embolic occlusion of a cervical or cerebral artery, leads to neurologic injury due to sudden disruption of blood flow to the brain. Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of disability and death and accounts for about 85% of strokes in the US.
OBSERVATIONS: Symptoms of acute ischemic stroke vary based on the area of the affected brain. Common presentations include sudden arm or leg weakness, aphasia or slurred speech, sudden loss of balance or coordination, sudden visual difficulties, and/or facial drooping. Patients with suspected stroke should be transported to the nearest emergency department for urgent brain imaging, typically noncontrast computed tomography (CT). Based on 2026 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA) guidelines, first-line therapy for patients with acute ischemic stroke presenting within 4.5 hours from symptom onset with disabling symptoms (eg, affecting the ability to perform activities of daily living) is intravenous thrombolysis (tenecteplase or alteplase) in those without intracranial hemorrhage or other contraindications to thrombolysis. The treatment window can be extended to 9 hours-and up to 24 hours in patients with large vessel occlusion (eg, involving the internal carotid artery or proximal middle cerebral artery [M1 segment]) who are unable to receive thrombectomy-based on identification of salvageable tissue using perfusion imaging with CT perfusion or magnetic resonance imaging. In appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, pooled randomized trial data show an approximately 10% absolute increase in the probability of a better functional outcome with intravenous thrombolysis. Based on 2026 AHA/ASA guidelines, endovascular thrombectomy, which involves clot removal with an intra-arterial mechanical device, is recommended for patients with large vessel occlusion within 6 hours of stroke onset (class 1 recommendation) and is recommended in selected patients with large vessel occlusion within 24 hours of last known well (class 1 recommendation). Endovascular therapy should be performed after intravenous thrombolysis unless patients have contraindications to thrombolytic therapy. Compared with medical management, which includes intravenous thrombolysis when indicated, endovascular thrombectomy produces an approximately 20% absolute increase in functional independence.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Acute ischemic stroke causes substantial disability and mortality. First-line therapy for patients with disabling acute stroke symptoms is intravenous thrombolysis (if no contraindications) within 4.5 hours of stroke onset and up to 24 hours in carefully selected patients not receiving mechanical thrombectomy; for large vessel occlusions, mechanical thrombectomy may be performed up to 24 hours after stroke onset in eligible patients.

items.title: Longitudinal change in FEV1 in adults with cystic fibrosis treated with elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor in France: a prospective observational study.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Without cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulators, cystic fibrosis is associated with an accelerated decline in percent predicted FEV1 (ppFEV1) of approximately 1·5% per year. Although treatment with elexacaftor-tezacaftor-ivacaftor (ETI) initially increases ppFEV1, little is known about its subsequent effect on ppFEV1 decline. Recent analyses of the extension phases of the phase 3 ETI pivotal studies found no evidence of ppFEV1 decline over 4 years in patients aged 12 years and older who were treated with ETI. The objective of this study was to examine the decline in ppFEV1 in a large, real-world cohort of adults with cystic fibrosis.
METHODS: Data from adults (aged ≥18 years) with cystic fibrosis and at least one F508del CFTR variant who initiated treatment with ETI between Dec 24, 2019, and Dec 23, 2023, at 31 cystic fibrosis centres included in the French prospective national observational ETI study in adults were analysed over 3 years. Eligible participants were those with at least three measures of ppFEV1 taken within 3 months following ETI initiation and the end of follow-up. The reference ppFEV1 was the highest ppFEV1 reached during the first 3 months of ETI treatment, after which subsequent decline in ppFEV1 was analysed by use of a linear mixed-effects model with random effects to estimate each participant's variation from the population mean.
FINDINGS: Data from 2321 adults with cystic fibrosis were included in this analysis. 1262 (54·4%) participants were male and 1059 (45·6%) were female. Median age was 29·2 years (IQR 23·1-36·7) and the pre-ETI initiation ppFEV1 was 59·7% (IQR 39·8-79·1). Within the first 3 months following ETI initiation, ppFEV1 increased by a median of 14·5 percentage points (IQR 7·9-22·7). The subsequent mean decline in ppFEV1 was 0·70% (95% CI 0·57-0·83) per year. Importantly, the decline in ppFEV1 was heterogeneous, with 1583 (68·2%) of 2321 participants showing no or limited decline (less than or equal to 1·5% per year). The remaining 738 (31·8%) participants showed a decline of greater than 1·5% per year, with 342 (46·3%) of these participants having a decline of greater than 3·0% per year. In multivariable analyses, the decline in ppFEV1 was greater in participants with a higher ppFEV1 at 3 months after ETI initiation. Treatment with oral azithromycin at 1 year after ETI initiation was associated with a lower risk of having a decline greater than 1·5% per year (relative risk 0·78 [95% CI 0·68-0·90]; p <0·01), as was treatment with inhaled antibiotics (0·81 [0·70-0·94]; p <0·01).
INTERPRETATION: These results suggest that approximately a third of adults with cystic fibrosis who are treated with ETI had a persistent decline in ppFEV1. These data emphasise the importance of regular ppFEV1 monitoring and highlight the need to improve current therapeutic strategies to prevent ppFEV1 decline. Proposed strategies could include use of newer CFTR modulators to restore CFTR function more effectively, as well as mucoactive, anti-infective, and anti-inflammatory therapies.

items.title: Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of intensive compared with standard treatment of systolic blood pressure (SBP) on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes.
DESIGN: Multicentre, open label, outcome assessor masked, randomised controlled trial.
SETTING: 145 clinical centres across seven geographical regions in China.
PARTICIPANTS: 12 821 adults aged ≥50 years with type 2 diabetes, raised SBP, and increased cardiovascular risk, of whom 12 434 without probable dementia at baseline were included in this cognitive ancillary study. Further assessments were performed annually and at the end of study.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned to receive intensive treatment targeting SBP <120 mm Hg or standard treatment targeting SBP <140 mm Hg for up to five years.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary cognitive outcome was a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Secondary cognitive outcomes included all cause dementia, mild cognitive impairment, changes in cognitive functions, and changes in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics. A subset of participants underwent brain MRI at baseline (n=862) and at the end of study (n=605) to assess changes in white matter lesion volume and total brain volume.
RESULTS: 6219 participants were assigned to receive intensive treatment and 6215 to receive standard treatment. Baseline mean age was 63.7 years, and 5567 (44.8%) participants were women. After one year, mean SBP was 121.6 mm Hg in the intensive treatment group and 133.2 mm Hg in the standard treatment group. During a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the primary cognitive outcome of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment occurred in 747 participants (3.69 events per 100 person years) in the intensive treatment group and 783 participants (3.89 events per 100 person years) in the standard treatment group (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 1.06; P=0.38). In the MRI substudy (428 intensive treatment v 434 standard treatment), the intensive treatment group had a smaller increase in white matter lesion volume compared with the standard treatment group (between group difference -0.09 inverse hyperbolic sine (asinh) transformed cm3, 95% CI -0.15 to -0.02; P=0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Over a median of about four years, no statistically significant difference in incidence of a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment was observed among adults with type 2 diabetes receiving standard treatment of SBP (target <140 mm Hg) and intensive treatment (target <120 mm Hg). Intensive treatment was, however, associated with a reduction in the accrual of cerebral white matter lesion volume.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03808311.

items.title: Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer.
items.abstract: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)-a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody-drug conjugate-has demonstrated efficacy in patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ± actionable genomic alterations. However, TROP2 expression by pathologist assessment using conventional immunohistochemistry with visual scoring does not predict response to TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugates in NSCLC. We developed TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring (QCS)-a fully supervised computational pathology approach that quantifies TROP2 expression in individual NSCLC cells and subcellular components from immunohistochemistry-stained slides. Using QCS to determine TROP2 expression at the tumor cell membrane and cytoplasm, normalized membrane ratio (NMR) was developed (ratio of membrane relative to membrane + cytoplasmic TROP2) in the biomarker-evaluable population of patients with advanced NSCLC in the TROPION-PanTumor01 study (n = 115). The TROP2 NMR cut-point was optimized and validated in patients with nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (primary intended-use population, n = 221) in the biomarker-evaluable population (n = 352) of the TROPION-Lung01 trial. Association with clinical outcomes was assessed. Progression-free survival was longer in Dato-DXd-treated (median 7.2 versus 4.0 months; hazard ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.64) but not docetaxel-treated (median 4.1 versus 4.4 months; hazard ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.59-1.49) patients with TROP2 NMR-positive versus TROP2 NMR-negative samples (treatment by biomarker status interaction P = 0.0098), indicating that TROP2 NMR may be a predictive biomarker for Dato-DXd.

items.title: Effect of discontinuing antihypertensives on perioperative hypotension in older patients before non-cardiac surgery: multicentre, randomised, double blind, controlled trial.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether discontinuing versus continuing angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) on the morning of surgery reduces perioperative hypotension in older patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery.
DESIGN: Multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled trial.
SETTING: Five tertiary teaching hospitals in China, November 2020 to December 2023.
PARTICIPANTS: 2036 older patients (60-80 years) using ACE inhibitors or ARBs for at least two weeks and scheduled for non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomised to receive their usual ACE inhibitor or ARB or a placebo in identical capsules on the morning of surgery.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was the incidence of perioperative hypotension (mean blood pressure <65 mm Hg or a ≥30% decrease from baseline requiring treatment). Secondary outcomes included duration of hypotension, requirement for a vasopressor, intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, and 30 day complications (neurocognitive disorders, major cardiocerebral events) or mortality.
RESULTS: 2012 patients (mean age 68.8 years; 54.4% male) completed the study: 1004 were included in the antihypertensive group and 1008 in the no antihypertensive group. The incidence of perioperative hypotension was lower in the no antihypertensive group (314/1008, 31.2%) versus antihypertensive group (457/1004, 45.5%): adjusted odds ratio 0.52 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.43 to 0.63); absolute risk difference -14.4% (95% CI -18.5% to -10.1%); P<0.001. The duration of hypotension and requirement for a vasopressor were both reduced in the no antihypertensive group: adjusted mean difference -1.3 minutes (95% CI -1.8 to -0.8 minutes) and 28.5% v 41.1%; adjusted odds ratio 0.54 (95% CI 0.44 to 0.66). Intraoperative fluid volume, postoperative hypotension, 30 day complications, and mortality did not differ significantly between groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Discontinuing ACE inhibitors or ARBs on the morning of surgery in older patients with hypertension statistically significantly reduced perioperative hypotension and the requirement for vasopressors without increasing 30 day complications or mortality. This simple strategy provides high certainty evidence for preoperative drug management in this patient population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2000039376.
